messages.subject: rmr program efficiency
parts:
Hi All,

 

I have a task to do, it need to pull the test from a file and do check on those words and count number of words( it is almost similar to word count. A few conditions added on them)

 

For this I wrote two different programs, both are working fine and giving the same result. Not sure which one is correct in terms of efficiency and load

 

Here is the first one: written an input format function to do the task

ur <- url('http://jmlr.org/papers/volume5/lewis04a/a11-smart-stop-list/english.stop',open="r") # Connection to a url has stopwords

stopwords <- readLines(ur) # reading stop words

close(ur) #Closing url connection

 

# Input format function to clean the text and get the desired output

input.format.custom <- function(con,nrecs)

{

  lines <- readLines(con,1)

  if (length(lines) == 0)

    NULL

  else {

    strings <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(lines, split="\\s+"))) # List of words in lower case

    ptrn <- '^http.*?'; ndx = grep(ptrn, strings, perl=T); strings[-ndx] # Identifying words starting with http and removing those words

    strings <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", strings) # Removing special characters

    StopwordMatch <- match(strings,c(stopwords,"","*")) #Customizing stopwords and matching with strings

    strings <- strings[is.na(StopwordMatch)] #Removing stopwords

    tOfwords <- tapply(strings,strings,length)

    Word.Count <- data.frame(Words=names(tOfwords),counts=unname(tOfwords))

    keyval(NULL,Word.Count)

  }

}

input.format.read = make.input.format(format = input.format.custom, mode = "text")

 

rmr.options(backend="hadoop")

d <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input='/hdfs/hdfp/NEWS',input.format=input.format.read,map=function(k,v) keyval(k,v)))

 

 

Here is the second one: written an map reduce function to do the task

ur <- url('http://jmlr.org/papers/volume5/lewis04a/a11-smart-stop-list/english.stop',open="r") # Connection to a url has stopwords

stopwords <- readLines(ur) # reading stop words

close(ur) #Closing url connection

 

# map  function to clean the text and get the desired output

tm.map <- function(con,nrecs)

{

    strings <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(nrecs, split="\\s+"))) # List of words in lower case

    ptrn <- '^http.*?'; ndx = grep(ptrn, strings, perl=T); strings[-ndx] # Identifying words starting with http and removing those words

    strings <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", strings) # Removing special characters

    StopwordMatch <- match(strings,c(stopwords,"","*")) #Customizing stopwords and matching with strings

    strings <- strings[is.na(StopwordMatch)] #Removing stopwords

    tOfwords <- tapply(strings,strings,length)

    Word.Count <- data.frame(Words=names(tOfwords),counts=unname(tOfwords))

    keyval(NULL,Word.Count)

}

 

rmr.options(backend="hadoop")

d <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input='/hdfs/hdfp/NEWS',input.format="text",map=tm.map))

  

Here are my question:

1.       Which program is efficient?

2.       If I use input format function to do the task, where the execution of cleaning is (is it in Hadoop or local)

 

Other points: you can ask me why I have done count of words map task and generate it value and key as null. The answer I observed was, input put file has ~50k words after splitting and when I pass all those words as keys my program returning an error message saying maximum limit of map task reached. So I kept it in a table and passed it as values.

 

One more observation:

I had used rmr.options to reset the # of map tasks as (rmr.options(backend="hadoop",backend.parameters=list(hadoop=list('D=mapred.reduce.tasks=10','D=mapred.map.tasks=100','D=mapred.tasktracker.map.tasks.maximum=1000'))) but this seems no effect on the process. I check the logs in ‘/logs/userlogs/job_201402011706_0047/’ directory I could see a job-acls.xml(this file exists in each job’s directory) file and it has some options set for the job. I feel this file should include those parameters what we set in the rmr.options statement, but not set in the file.

 

Please help me.


Regards,

Sivaji
